name: humanize-intcomma-zero-digits-preserves-integers
rationale: humanize 4.16.0 documents intcomma as inserting separators into an integer, and ndigits as precision for rounding after the decimal point. Therefore ndigits=0 on an exact integer must preserve its integer digits. The official release tests cover intcomma('1234567', 1), confirming that precision is accepted for integer inputs. The independent oracle groups str(abs(n)) into three-digit chunks without float conversion or a numeric format specifier. Official contract and release source: https://humanize.readthedocs.io/en/stable/number/#humanize.number.intcomma and https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/blob/3c577d7650508d52aa2982e930b0e744c343082f/src/humanize/number.py .
domain: Python int inputs across the signed 64-bit interval, -2**63 through 2**63-1; fresh process default English locale; ndigits fixed to 0. Excludes floats, fractional values, strings, custom locales, negative precision, and integers outside the stated bound. Since inputs are exact integers with no fractional digits, no intended decimal rounding is needed.
